div.div:
Why this is one report and not five calls
Until 0.6.0 each consumer assembled the same five-term disjunction itself,
and both did: the CLI and the GUI carried near-identical copies, comments
included, while only three of the five axes were library code at all.
Two copies of one rule in two repositories is one place for a sixth axis to
be added on one side and silently forgotten on the other — and the forgotten
side keeps shipping stale output without saying anything.
The axes stay separate rather than collapsing into a single flag because a
consumer needs more than the verdict: the CLI prints which setting moved.

switch.text: Why this is one report and not five calls...

div.div:
What a hash can never see
Editing a canvas profile's margins changes neither the input files nor the
output files — both stay byte-identical — yet every affected page renders
differently. The same is true of reordering inputs, of switching output
format, and of enabling a grade. That is the whole reason the five settings
axes exist: content hashing is necessary and not remotely sufficient.

div.div:
A shrinking chapter orphans files
A margin edit changes page height, so strip height, so the slice COUNT.
Ten slices can become eight, leaving output_009 and output_010 behind
under names the new settings never produce. Any consumer that deletes
what a render no longer generates must do so on every configuration
change, not only on a format switch.

a.text: Text is not SVG - cannot display
